heads.message:
prefill: gather Engram rows on a helper thread at chunk start (DSX_ENGRAM_PREFETCH, default on)

Rows depend only on token ids, so both Engram layers' rows (layer 1 first) are hashed and gathered while the GPUs
run the layers before them instead of inline at layers 1 and 14. Logits byte-identical. 8K prefill on .102
(base vs prefetch, order-swapped): repetitive fixture cold 918 -> 954 tok/s (+3.9%), warm 1001 -> 1016 (+1.5%);
8K code prompt cold 792 -> 866 (+9.4%), warm 919 -> 937 (+2.0%). Profiled waits for rows: 0 ms.

material_new_prs.title: ds4: an expert gives the same bits on the CPU lane and in VRAM (opt-in, #644)
material_new_prs.author: cresslank
material_new_prs.head: c1a134d1100d288518eeb95378f3b91ab885b2f8
material_new_prs.body:
Fixes #644 for Maya-S's expert types, behind a new opt-in setting, `MAYA_DS4_LANE_PARITY=1`. With it off (the default), output is bit-for-bit the same as v1.1.45.

### What this does

As soon as one routed expert sits in RAM, two runs of the same greedy request can give different answers. On a single 24-48 GB card that's most experts (91% on the L40S in #644). So outputs can't be compared: an upgrade check or `--multi-check` can't tell a real change from placement noise, and a bug report can't be reproduced, because the reporter's placement and expert-cache history are part of the input.

It happens with every expert in VRAM too. Long prompts give different logits after a restart, because the expert profile's update moves experts between VRAM slots. So an agent run can't be replayed exactly.

With the setting on, the answer depends only on the input. It doesn't make answers better or faster: perplexity is unchanged (16.83 vs 16.84), and the costs are under Speed.

### Causes

@talisp traced #644 to the expert cache moving experts between the CPU lane and VRAM, and @pattalkslaw-del showed the expert profile changes the logits too. Five things tied an expert's output to where it sat:

- The CPU lane sums a row's blocks in ggml's order, not the GPU kernel's.
- The SwiGLU uses the CPU's `exp` on the lane and CUDA's `expf` on the GPU. `expf` goes through `ex2.approx`, which a CPU can't reproduce.
- The lane's experts join the expert sum as one vector after the VRAM experts, so the sum's order follows the placement.
- The chunked prompt pass sums experts set by set in placement order, and only VRAM experts get the busy-expert FP16 GEMMs.
- The prompt path (chunked pass or windows of 16) is chosen by timing, and the two round differently.

### Changes

With the setting on:

- CPU-lane rows for IQ2_XXS, IQ2_S, IQ3_XXS and IQ3_S use the GPU kernel's arithmetic: Q8_K activations, the same lane split (32 lanes per gate/up row, 16 per down row) and the same reduction order. The integer dots use AVX2, checked against a scalar version on first use (`src/ds4/ds4_lane_parity.cpp`).
- The SwiGLU uses a portable `exp` on both sides, within 1 ulp of e^x for x >= -87 (`src/ds4/ds4_par_exp.h`).
- Each CPU-lane expert's output goes into the sum at its own pick's position, as it would from VRAM.
- The chunked pass sums experts exactly in 64-bit fixed point, so set order doesn't matter, and streamed busy experts get the FP16 GEMMs too.
- The prompt path is chosen by length unless `MAYA_DS4_PROMPT_PICK` is set.

### Results

2x RTX PRO 6000 with a layer split, Ryzen 9 9950X3D, Maya-S, greedy. I moved experts to the CPU lane with `--reserve-mib`.

| | v1.1.45 | Setting on |
|---|---|---|
| 3 runs each with 0, ~400 and ~790 experts on the CPU lane | Runs with experts on the lane differ from each other and from the all-VRAM run | All 9 identical (logits and 48 tokens) |
| `--parallel 2 --multi-check` | 45/79 rows identical (16 experts on the lane), 0/47 (362) | 94/94 (50), 94/94 (430) |
| 3,000-token prompt | Differs between placements, and between restarts with every expert in VRAM | Identical at every placement and across restarts |
| Perplexity, 8 x 1,024 tokens | 16.84 all in VRAM, 16.95 with 722 on the lane | 16.83 at both |

With the setting off, logits match v1.1.45 bit for bit: with every expert in VRAM, with 299 experts on the lane and `--no-expert-cache`, and through the chunked pass with `--expert-profile none`.

With the setting on, output changes slightly even with every expert in VRAM, because of the new `exp` and the exact sums. On the synthetic prompt from #644, the last logits move by up to 3.3, with the same top token.

### Speed

| | v1.1.45 | Setting on |
|---|---|---|
| Decode, every expert in VRAM | 80.2, 80.8 tok/s | 80.7, 80.6 |
| Same, DSpark on | 98.6 | 101.9 |
| Decode, 720-790 experts on the CPU lane | 78.3, 77.6 | 72.2, 74.2 |
| 3,000-token prompt, every expert in VRAM | 1.10 s | 1.15 s |
| Same, 720-790 experts on the CPU lane | 1.40-1.46 s | 1.45-1.50 s |

Decode is 384 tokens of an essay with prompt lookup off. For the rows with experts on the CPU lane, I turned the PCIe lane off on both builds (`MAYA_DS4_STREAM=0`). A bad cached timing in `lane-times.txt` had switched it on for this build, costing 25-30% of decode with the setting on or off.

The costs are why it's opt-in:

- The new CPU rows are slower than ggml's on one thread: 1.4-1.6x per IQ2_XXS expert, 2.3-2.8x per IQ2_S (`ds4_par_bench`). Few picks reach the lane on real text (330 of 91,920 above), but a card with most experts in RAM would notice.
- The exact sum needs 335 MB of VRAM per GPU at the default 8,192-token chunk, about 30 fewer experts per GPU.

### Not covered yet

- Other expert types on the CPU lane (MXFP4, EXL3, IQ1_S/IQ1_M, IQ4_XS, IQ4_NL) and mixed layers.
- The helper GPU, tensor-parallel groups and `DS4_SYNC=1`.
- AMD, where the setting is ignored: the new rows copy the CUDA kernels, and I can't test HIP.
- A prompt longer than one chunk can still differ between configurations, because chunk size depends on free VRAM at load.

### Overlap

- #736: one small conflict in `ds4_model.cu`, right after `flow_layer`. Whichever lands second keeps both lines, with the exact-sum finish before the all-reduce.
- #641 changes which `Resp` slot a window uses, and the new per-pick buffer would need to follow it. #641 already conflicts with main.
- #636 freezes the expert cache during `--multi-check`. With this setting on, the check passes without that.
- No other open PR conflicts with this one.

This builds on v1.1.18's Q8_K activations (#312) and is the same kind of fix as #608. talisp's comment on #644 links a similar fix in Colibri (JustVugg/colibri#1146).

### Testing

- `ds4_gguf_test --parity` (new, also in the default run) checks the portable `exp` on host and device (550,773 inputs, none differ) and the new rows against the GPU kernels, bit for bit, for 4 type pairs at 3 sizes. The full `ds4_gguf_test` passes: 585 checks, against 572 on main.
- `ds4_par_bench` (built by name) times the new rows against ggml's.
- The CI checks pass locally: `tools/check_hip_compat.py`, the GLM memory test, the server tests and the installer and tools tests.
- Built for sm_120 with CUDA 13.2 and g++ 15. Not built on Windows or AMD; the CPU code uses the same MSVC calls as `ds4_iq_cpu.cpp`.
- The end-to-end checks compare `DS4_DUMP_LAST` files from `maya-ds4 --ids` runs.

material_new_prs.title: ds4: add opt-in direct NH copies for RAM-tier prompt flow
material_new_prs.author: oscarlius
material_new_prs.head: 550a6ca977b348fbc3e583258ec9575c02ed48f4
material_new_prs.body:
Copied RAM-tier MXFP4 experts currently assemble their host parts in a staging slot before the prompt-flow H2D copy. This adds an opt-in path that copies each part directly into the same ring destination, removing that CPU staging copy for eligible experts.

`MAYA_DS4_FLOW_DIRECT_NH=1` is off by default. It requires registered copied host memory, a single-member layer, an available RAM copy, and matrix row counts divisible by `NH`. Ineligible items retain the existing path. Ring ownership and completion events are unchanged; no new CUDA APIs are introduced. The settings table and README link document the measured scope.

### Historical before/after evidence

Measured on 2026-10-31 UTC: v1.1.43 (`acdab34`), four RTX 4090 24 GB at 265 W, dual Xeon Platinum 8380 / two NUMA nodes, about 251 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4. Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GSQ-RCO-IQ2_XXS. Chunk 8192, context 262144, parallel capacity 8, DSpark on. All three arms used the same instrumented experimental binary and frozen profile, with direct copies off/on/off; other experiments were disabled.

| Input | Paired Prefill change | Paired Decode change | A2/A1 Decode drift |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K | +3.61% | +2.40% | -0.80% |
| 8K | +0.88% | +1.21% | +1.30% |
| 32K | +0.90% | +0.60% | +2.32% |

Each row is the median of two different fixed inputs, comparing each B result with the geometric mean of its matching A1/A2 controls. These are bounded observations, not statistical significance or a general speedup claim. Decode changes are not causally established by this prompt-copy experiment.

- 30 candidate requests plus one restoration probe; no eight-client load run.
- All six performance inputs had matching generated-output hashes across the three arms. JSON, warmup and completed resumption outputs also matched. Broad quality and numerical equivalence are unproven.
- The historical instrumented build recorded direct-copy activity on all four GPUs and 17 passing device-format copy/boundary fixtures. Counters measure enqueued bytes, not PCIe bandwidth.
- The committed [case study](https://github.com/oscarlius/project-maya/blob/perf/ds4-direct-nh-dma-20261101/docs/benchmarks/ds41-direct-nh-v1143-20261031.md) includes all 30 sanitized sample records, input payloads, hashes, arm settings and limitations.

### Submission validation

This patch is adapted to v1.1.46 `main` (`3589d6f`). The newer upstream diagnostic callers retain their existing behavior through default arguments. The old measurement instrumentation and unrelated experimental features are not included.

**No tests or builds were run for this submission.** The historical v1.1.43 evidence does not validate this submitted commit. Read-only review found no definite blocking issue, but the existing TP/flow-copy diagnostic calls do not exercise the new `direct=true` branch. Current CUDA/HIP builds, runtime regression coverage, V100/Windows behavior and required CI remain unverified.

Ready for review of this narrow opt-in approach. It does not change defaults, claim current-main acceptance, or combine gains with the separate chunk-size documentation in #650.
